# Q2 - How Does It Read On One Slide?

**A.** As one row of four. The point of the slide is not the feature list -
it is that a reader gets the shape of the year in one line and can hold it
in their head while the detail is explained.

| | | | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Q1** | **BUILD** | Define MVP | Core workflows | Initial testing | **MVP Ready** |
| **Q2** | **INTEGRATE** | Connect ecosystem | AI & matching | Pilot preparation | **Pilot Ready** |
| **Q3** | **PILOT** | Real institutions | User adoption | Feedback & refinement | **Validated Product** |
| **Q4** | **LAUNCH** | Market readiness | Paying customers | Scale strategy | **Market Ready** |

![The one-year plan](../_exports/charts/questions/q_01_roadmap_slide.png)

## The story, in four words

**Q1 → Build · Q2 → Integrate · Q3 → Validate · Q4 → Launch**

That is stronger for an investor than a long list of technical features,
because it is a sequence rather than a catalogue. Every feature in the
roadmap is defensible only as a contribution to one of those four words.

## What the slide is not

It is not the whole argument. The slide says **what happens when**. The
budget says **what it costs**, and [Q3](03_Budget.md) is where a reader
checks that the two agree.

| | Quarter | The slide says | The budget says |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | **BUILD** | Define MVP, Core workflows | Rs 1,35,000 — 67% of it technology |
| Q2 | **INTEGRATE** | Connect ecosystem, AI & matching | Rs 1,50,000 — 53% technology, 37% in the other lines |
| Q3 | **PILOT** | Real institutions, User adoption | Rs 1,65,000 — 21% market research, the year's peak |
| Q4 | **LAUNCH** | Market readiness, Paying customers | Rs 1,50,000 — 27% market research, 17% contingency | |

## One thing to say out loud

**"Every expense answers one question: what milestone does this money help
us achieve?"**

If an expense cannot be tied to one of the four milestones, it does not go
in this budget. That single test is what turns a list of costs into a
defensible request.
